mainTopic: Covering a beehive on שבת, making shade for a מת, and whether טלטול מן הצד counts as moving
overview: The amud first finishes the question of covering a beehive on שבת without breaking רבי יצחק's rule that a כלי may only be moved for something that may itself be moved. In summer the covering is for the honey. In the rainy season it is for the two honeycombs left for the bees, as long as the owner had them in mind before שבת so they are not מוקצה. The גמרא then shows that the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and that ״שלא יתכוין לצוד״ means leaving a gap so the mat does not trap the bees. רב אשי answers differently: the ברייתא means sunny and rainy days in ניסן and תשרי, when there is honey. Next, רב ששת says רב הונא already taught רבי יצחק's idea: a מחיצה may be made for a מת for the sake of the living, but not for the sake of the מת. A ברייתא shows how two people can leave a shade over a corpse in the sun indirectly. Then רב and שמואל argue about how to move such a corpse, which comes down to whether טלטול מן הצד counts as moving. The גמרא tries to link this to a dispute of תנאים about rescuing a corpse from a fire, but rejects the link. רבי יהודה בן לקיש's reason is a person's panic over his מת, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The summer case works because there is honey
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes the earlier answer: in summer the covering is allowed because the hive contains honey.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of an answer that started on the previous amud. In summer the hive has honey, so the mat is a covering for the honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק forbids making a covering for something forbidden to move on שבת. The bees are forbidden to move, but the honey is permitted food. So covering the hive counts as covering the honey, and רבי יצחק has no problem with it.

phrases.english: Since there is honey [in the hive in summer].
phrases.notes: This continues the answer on the previous amud: in summer the covering is for the honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer, begun earlier on the daf, that defends the ברייתא against רבי יצחק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the covering is really for the honey.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Covering the hive looks like making a covering for the bees, which are מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In summer the covering is for the honey, which is permitted.

steps.title: What about the rainy season, when there is no honey?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the honey answer: in winter there is no honey, so what is being covered?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the rainy season, when there is no honey, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The ברייתא also allows covering the hive in the rain, and in winter there is no honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honey answer only works in summer. The ברייתא's words ״ובגשמים מפני הגשמים״ seem to permit covering in the rainy season too. Then the only thing left to cover is the bees, and that brings back רבי יצחק's problem.

keyTerms.meaning: What can be said? (a formula that demands an answer)

phrases.english: In the rainy season, when there is no honey,
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the honey answer by pointing to the winter case in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the covering is for the honey.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In winter there is no honey, yet the ברייתא still permits covering. So the honey cannot be what justifies it.

steps.title: The two honeycombs left for winter
steps.stepSummary: Even in winter, two honeycombs are left in the hive for the bees to eat, and the covering is for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for those two honeycombs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that some honey is still there in winter. Beekeepers leave two honeycombs inside so the bees can feed, and the mat covers those.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honey answer is kept, but adjusted for winter. There is still permitted food in the hive, the two leftover combs, so the covering is not just for the bees.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (narrowing the case)

phrases.english: It is needed only
phrases.notes: The גמרא is limiting the winter case to one specific situation.

phrases.english: for those two honeycombs.
phrases.notes: The combs left in the hive so the bees can eat during winter.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לְאוֹתָן שְׁתֵּי חַלּוֹת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: in winter the covering is for the two leftover combs.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In winter there is no honey at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two combs always stay in the hive, so there is still honey to cover.

steps.title: But those combs are מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the two combs are set aside for the bees, so they are מוקצה and cannot justify the covering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the two-combs answer. Those combs are meant for the bees, not for people, so they should count as מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner does not plan to eat those combs; they are left for the bees. Food set aside like that is מוקצה on שבת. If so, it is as forbidden as the bees, and covering it brings back רבי יצחק's problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside; forbidden to use or move on שבת

phrases.english: But they are set aside [מוקצה]!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the two combs make the covering permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The combs are set aside for the bees, so they are מוקצה. Covering a מוקצה item is the very thing רבי יצחק forbids.

steps.title: He had the combs in mind before שבת
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the owner thought about using the combs before שבת, so they are not מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where he had them in mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the owner planned before שבת that he might eat these combs. That plan removes the מוקצה status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוקצה depends on what a person expects to use. Once the owner had the combs in mind as possible food, they become permitted. So covering them is allowed, just like the summer honey.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought about them / designated them in his mind for use

phrases.english: Where he had them in mind [before שבת].
phrases.notes: Planning before שבת to eat them removes the מוקצה status.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to one where the owner made a mental designation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The combs are automatically מוקצה because they are left for the bees.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the owner had them in mind before שבת, they are not מוקצה.

steps.title: So without that thought it would be forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the logical inference: if he did not have them in mind, covering the hive would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: So if he did not have them in mind, what then? It is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא states what follows from the last answer: without the owner's thought, covering would be forbidden. It is preparing a challenge from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the permission depends on the owner thinking about the combs, then the ruling must reverse when he did not. The גמרא puts this conclusion on the table so it can ask why the ברייתא never mentions it.

keyTerms.meaning: But if not… (draws an inference from the opposite case)

phrases.english: But if he did not have them in mind,
what then — it is forbidden?
phrases.notes: This is really a conclusion said as a question; the גמרא accepts it and uses it in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא חַשֵּׁיב עֲלַיְיהוּ מַאי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out what the previous answer implies, as setup for a challenge.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the ruling flips to forbidden when the owner did not think about the combs.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Implied yes: it would be forbidden. The next step builds on this.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא should have stated that distinction
steps.stepSummary: If the permission depends on the owner's thought, the ברייתא should have said so instead of adding the trapping clause.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the one who taught 'as long as he does not intend to trap' should have made a distinction in this case itself: when is this said? When he had them in mind. But if he did not have them in mind, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the two-combs answer from the wording of the ברייתא. The ברייתא adds a condition about trapping, but it never adds the more important condition about thinking ahead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא was willing to add one condition, ״ובלבד שלא יתכוין לצוד״. If having the combs in mind were also required, it should have said so in the same place. Its silence suggests the two-combs explanation is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it make a distinction and teach it within this very case
In what case is this said? (a limiting formula)

phrases.english: If so, the one who taught:
'As long as he does not intend to trap'
— let him distinguish and teach within this case itself:
In what case are these words said?
— when he had them in mind;
but if he did not have them in mind — it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 6 to attack the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two-combs answer together with its condition that the owner had them in mind.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already adds a condition about trapping. A more basic condition about thinking ahead should have been stated too, and it is missing.

steps.title: The trapping clause adds something even when he had them in mind
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is teaching that even when he had the combs in mind, covering is allowed only if he does not intend to trap.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us: even though he had them in mind, it is allowed only as long as he does not intend to trap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא worded things this way. It is already talking about the case where he had the combs in mind, and it adds that even then he must not intend to trap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes the permitted case, where he had the combs in mind. Its new point is the extra condition: designating the combs does not remove the trapping concern. So the trapping clause is the real lesson, and nothing is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
even though he had them in mind,
it is only as long as he does not intend to trap.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the clause as a new point (חידוש) that applies on top of the permitted case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trapping clause looks like the only condition, so the 'had them in mind' condition seems absent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is speaking of the case where he had them in mind and adds the trapping restriction on top of it.

steps.title: Whose view is this ברייתא? Neither רבי שמעון nor רבי יהודה seems to fit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the ברייתא follows. רבי שמעון has no מוקצה, and רבי יהודה forbids even unintended acts.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If רבי שמעון, he does not hold of מוקצה. If רבי יהודה, what difference does it make that he does not intend? An unintended act is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the ברייתא itself. It cannot match רבי שמעון, because the whole discussion assumed מוקצה. It cannot match רבי יהודה, because he does not care whether the person intends to trap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון rejects מוקצה here, so the two-combs discussion would be pointless for him. רבי יהודה holds דבר שאין מתכוין אסור: an act that may cause a forbidden result is forbidden even without intent. So for him the phrase 'as long as he does not intend' makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who rejects מוקצה here and permits unintended acts
A תנא who holds of מוקצה and forbids unintended acts
An act done without intent for the forbidden result

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two תנאים. רבי שמעון permits דבר שאין מתכוין and has no מוקצה. רבי יהודה forbids דבר שאין מתכוין and does hold of מוקצה.

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּי? אִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן — לֵית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה.
phrases.english: Whose view is this? If רבי שמעון — he does not hold of מוקצה.
If רבי יהודה —
when he does not intend, what difference does it make?
An unintended act is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts to asking which תנא the ברייתא follows, given the מוקצה and intent issues just raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the ברייתא can be attributed to any known תנא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma: מוקצה rules out רבי שמעון, and the reliance on lack of intent rules out רבי יהודה.

steps.title: It follows רבי יהודה: do not make the mat into a trap
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. 'Not intending to trap' means arranging the mat so it does not work as a trap.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is רבי יהודה. What does 'as long as he does not intend to trap' mean? That he should not make it like a trap, by leaving them an opening so they do not get trapped by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps רבי יהודה and reinterprets the clause. It is not about what the person is thinking. It tells him how to place the mat: leave a gap so the bees are not caught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה intent does not matter, so the clause must describe a physical action. Leaving open space means no trapping happens at all. That removes the דבר שאין מתכוין problem, and the מוקצה discussion still fits רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. ״שלא יתכוין לצוד״ means leaving a gap so the mat does not act as a trap; it is not about mental intent.

phrases.english: Really, it is רבי יהודה.
What does 'as long as he does not intend to trap' mean?
— that he should not make it like a trap,
by leaving them an open space
so that they do not get trapped by themselves.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the clause from mental intent to a physical arrangement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not intend' refers to the person's thoughts, which do not matter to רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means physically leaving a gap so that no trapping happens.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא means ניסן and תשרי, when there is always honey
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads the ברייתא as describing sun and rain within one season, ניסן and תשרי, when the hive has honey, so the winter problem never arises.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Does it say 'in the summer and in the rainy season'? It says 'in the sun because of the sun and in the rain because of the rain', meaning the days of ניסן and תשרי, when there is sun and cold, rain and honey.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different answer to the winter question from step 2. He says the ברייתא never mentioned winter. It means sunny days and rainy days during ניסן and תשרי, when the hive still has honey.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's words describe the weather, not the season of the year. In the transitional months there are both sunny and rainy days, and honey is present the whole time. So the honey answer works on its own, and there is no need for the two combs, the מוקצה issue, or the owner's thought.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it actually say…? (rejects a reading of the text)
The months of ניסן and תשרי, the spring and fall seasons

steps.whyThisMatters: רב אשי's reading makes the whole chain of steps 3–8 unnecessary. It keeps the simple honey explanation of why covering the hive does not conflict with רבי יצחק.
steps.whatToRemember: Two approaches answer the winter problem. The first says the covering is for the two combs the owner had in mind. רב אשי says the ברייתא only means ניסן and תשרי, when honey is present.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
Does it teach 'in the summer and in the rainy season'?
'In the sun because of the sun
and in the rain because of the rain' is what it teaches,
in the days of ניסן and the days of תשרי,
when there is sun and there is cold,
and there is rain and there is honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the winter challenge in step 2 and answers it a different way, without the two-combs approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא's wording: the clauses describe weather, not seasons.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״ובגשמים״ refers to the winter season, when there is no honey.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means rainy days in ניסן and תשרי, when honey is present, so covering is always for the honey.

steps.title: רב ששת says רב הונא already taught רבי יצחק's rule
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת sends word to רבי יצחק that רב הונא already taught his rule in בבל. You may make a מחיצה for a מת for the sake of the living, but not for the sake of the מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: Go and tell רבי יצחק that רב הונא already explained your teaching in בבל. רב הונא said: You may make a partition for a dead body for the sake of a living person, but you may not make a partition for a dead body for the sake of the dead person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the rule of רבי יצחק: a כלי may be moved only for the sake of something that may itself be moved on שבת. רב ששת says this is not new, because רב הונא already taught the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מת is מוקצה and may not be moved on שבת. So according to רב הונא, you may not carry a mat or other כלי just to benefit the מת, though you may do it for a living person. This matches רבי יצחק exactly: a כלי may not be moved for the sake of something that is itself forbidden to move.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition or covering; here, a shade put over a corpse
A dead body, which is מוקצה on שבת
For the sake of a living person
He explained it / already taught it

steps.whyThisMatters: It connects רבי יצחק's general rule about moving כלים to a concrete case. That case leads into the whole discussion of a מת on שבת that follows.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them:
Go out and say to Rabbi Yitzchak:
Rav Huna already explained
phrases.notes: Meaning: your idea is not new.

phrases.english: your teaching, in Babylonia.
For Rav Huna said:
One may make a partition for a dead body for the sake of a living person,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין עוֹשִׂין מְחִיצָה לְמֵת בִּשְׁבִיל מֵת.
phrases.english: but one may not make a partition for a dead body for the sake of the dead person.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּבָר תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב הוּנָא לִשְׁמַעְתָּיךְ בְּבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It leaves the beehive discussion and goes back to רבי יצחק's rule from earlier on the daf.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's rule that a כלי may be moved only for the sake of something that may itself be moved
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's ruling that a מחיצה may be made for a מת for the sake of the living, but not for the sake of the מת

steps.title: What case is רב הונא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical case רב הונא's rule refers to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short clarifying question. It is setting up the next step, which brings a ברייתא showing the exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule is abstract. How do you make a partition 'for the living' when it really ends up shading the dead? The גמרא wants a concrete case that shows how this works.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (a request for the concrete case)

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks for the practical case behind רב הונא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical case in which a מחיצה is made for a מת for the sake of the living

steps.title: Two people shade a corpse indirectly
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes two people sitting by a corpse in the sun. They bring beds and a mat for their own comfort, then stand the beds up and slip away. A shade is left over the corpse on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה said, and שילא מרי taught the same: A dead body is lying in the sun. Two people come and sit beside it. When they feel hot from below, each one brings a bed and sits on it. When they feel hot from above, they bring a mat and spread it over themselves. Then each one stands his bed upright, slips out, and leaves. The partition ends up made by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows how a shade can end up over a corpse, even though the beds and mat were only brought for the living people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beds and mat are carried for the comfort of the two living people, so carrying them is allowed. When the people leave, the mat stays propped on the standing beds and shades the מת. No one ever carried a כלי directly for the מת. This shows רב הונא's rule: for the living it is allowed, for the dead it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: A corpse lying in the sun

steps.whatToRemember: A כלי may not be moved directly for a מת on שבת. But if it is moved for the living, and the מת ends up benefiting, that is allowed.

phrases.english: As Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said,
and so too Sheila Mari taught:
A corpse lying in the sun:

phrases.aramaic: בָּאִים שְׁנֵי בְּנֵי אָדָם וְיוֹשְׁבִין בְּצִדּוֹ.
phrases.english: two people come and sit beside it.
When they are hot from below,
this one brings a bed and sits on it,
and that one brings a bed and sits on it.
When they are hot from above,
they bring a mat and spread it over themselves.
This one stands his bed upright
and slips away and leaves,
and that one stands his bed upright
and slips away and leaves,
and the partition turns out to be made by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה, וְכֵן תָּנָא שֵׁילָא מָרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the question 'מאי היא' with a concrete ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is two people who shade themselves with beds and a mat, then leave. The shade remains over the מת indirectly.

steps.title: רב and שמואל argue about moving a corpse out of the sun
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says to move the corpse from bed to bed. רב says to place a loaf or a baby on it and then carry it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said about a corpse lying in the sun: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: You roll it from one bed to the next. רב חנינא בר שלמיא said in the name of רב: You place a loaf of bread or a baby on it, and then carry it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new מחלוקת between אמוראים about the same case: a corpse lying in the sun. Here the question is how to actually move the corpse into the shade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allows shifting the body from bed to bed, which is an indirect way of moving it. רב requires placing a permitted item on it, a loaf or a baby, so that the body becomes a base for something that may be moved. Then the whole thing may be carried for the sake of that permitted item.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
He turns it over from bed to bed
A loaf of bread or a baby

phrases.english: It was stated: a corpse lying in the sun.
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
One turns it over from bed to bed.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חֲנִינָא בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Chanina bar Shelamya said in the name of Rav:
One places a loaf or a baby on it
and moves it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It moves from the topic of a corpse in the sun to a related מחלוקת about how to move the corpse itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: move the corpse bed to bed. רב: place a loaf or a baby on it and carry it.

steps.title: Defining the dispute: does indirect moving count as moving?
steps.stepSummary: When a loaf or baby is available, everyone allows it. They argue only when there is none: is טלטול מן הצד considered moving?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where there is a loaf or a baby, everyone agrees it is allowed. They argue where there is none. One master holds that indirect moving counts as moving, and the other master holds that it does not count as moving.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down exactly where רב and שמואל disagree. They are not arguing about the loaf-or-baby method; they are arguing about a case where no loaf or baby is available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that טלטול מן הצד is still real moving, so rolling the body bed to bed is forbidden; you need a loaf or a baby. שמואל holds that indirect moving is not real moving, so rolling bed to bed is allowed. This turns their practical disagreement into a clear general principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Moving something in an indirect, unusual way

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב forbids what שמואל permits in every case. When a loaf or baby is available, both agree the body may be moved that way. The argument is only about a case without one.
steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת of רב and שמואל comes down to one question: is טלטול מן הצד considered moving? רב says yes, שמואל says no.

phrases.english: Where there is a loaf or a baby,
everyone agrees that it is permitted.
Where they argue is when he does not have one:

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר טִלְטוּל מִן הַצַּד שְׁמֵיהּ טִלְטוּל,
phrases.english: one master holds that moving indirectly counts as moving,
and the other master holds that it does not count as moving.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא כִּכָּר אוֹ תִּינוֹק כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains the principle behind the מחלוקת quoted in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone permits moving the corpse with a loaf or baby on it. Without one, רב forbids it because טלטול מן הצד counts as moving, and שמואל permits it because it does not.

steps.title: A proposal that תנאים argued the same point about a fire
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that this argument is the same as a תנאים dispute about saving a corpse from a fire on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is like a dispute of תנאים? The first view says: You may not rescue a dead body from a fire. רבי יהודה בן לקיש said: I heard that you may rescue a dead body from a fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that רב and שמואל are repeating an older argument between תנאים. It quotes the ברייתא, and it is setting up the next step, where it will try to prove the connection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא forbids rescuing a corpse from a fire on שבת, and רבי יהודה בן לקיש permits it. The גמרא suspects that this dispute is also about טלטול מן הצד. That would give רב and שמואל earlier sources for their views.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this matches a dispute of תנאים?
A תנא who permits rescuing the corpse

phrases.english: Shall we say it is like a dispute of tannaim?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַצִּילִין אֶת הַמֵּת מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה.
phrases.english: One may not rescue a corpse from a fire.
Rabbi Yehuda ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁמַּצִּילִין אֶת הַמֵּת מִפְּנֵי הַדְּלֵיקָה.
phrases.english: I heard that one may rescue a corpse from a fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It tries to link the רב–שמואל principle to an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that רב and שמואל's dispute about טלטול מן הצד is the same as a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about rescuing a corpse from a fire

steps.title: Proving the fire dispute must be about indirect moving
steps.stepSummary: If a loaf or baby were there, why would the תנא קמא forbid it? If none were there, why would רבי יהודה בן לקיש permit it? So they must be arguing about טלטול מן הצד.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If a loaf or baby is there, what is the reason of the תנא קמא for forbidding it? If there is none, what is the reason of רבי יהודה בן לקיש for permitting it? Rather, they must be arguing about indirect moving. One master holds that indirect moving counts as moving, and the other holds that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds the proof for its proposal. It shows that both simple ways of reading the case fail, so the only option left is that they argue about טלטול מן הצד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a loaf or baby, everyone permits moving the body, so the תנא קמא's ban would make no sense. Without one, moving the body directly is plainly forbidden, so רבי יהודה בן לקיש's permission would make no sense. The only way left to understand the ברייתא is that they argue about indirect moving, just like רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה
Rather, is it not that... (introduces the forced conclusion)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If there is a loaf or a baby,
what is the reason of the first tanna (for forbidding)?
If there is none,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לָקִישׁ?
phrases.english: what is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda ben Lakish (for permitting)?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּטִלְטוּל מִן הַצַּד פְּלִיגִי.
phrases.english: Rather, is it not that they argue about indirect moving?

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר טִלְטוּל מִן הַצַּד שְׁמֵיהּ טִלְטוּל,
phrases.english: One master holds that indirect moving counts as moving,
and the other master holds that it does not count as moving!
phrases.notes: רבי יהודה בן לקיש, like שמואל.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי: אִי דְּאִיכָּא כִּכָּר אוֹ תִּינוֹק, מַאי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the reasoning that supports the proposal in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That the תנאים argue about טלטול מן הצד, just like רב and שמואל
steps.raayaSupportSource: Ruling out both other readings of the ברייתא (with a loaf or baby, and without one)

steps.title: Rejection: everyone agrees indirect moving counts as moving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Both תנאים agree that טלטול מן הצד is moving, and רבי יהודה בן לקיש has a different reason: a person is panicked about his dead relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that indirect moving counts as moving. This is the reason of רבי יהודה בן לקיש: since a person is frantic about his dead relative...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against its own proposal. The תנאים do not argue about טלטול מן הצד; רבי יהודה בן לקיש permits the rescue for a separate reason. That reason continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the idea that רבי יהודה בן לקיש could only permit the rescue if he holds that indirect moving is not moving. The גמרא gives him a different reason: a person is overwhelmed with worry about the honor of his מת. So the ruling about the fire is a special case and does not prove the general principle. The sentence is cut off here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: This passage ends in the middle of a sentence. The full reason of רבי יהודה בן לקיש (what the רבנן allowed because of this panic) comes in the next part of the גמרא.

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees that
indirect moving counts as moving,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: and this is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda ben Lakish:
since a person is frantic about his dead relative
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא טִלְטוּל מִן הַצַּד שְׁמֵיהּ טִלְטוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the proof from step 18 by giving רבי יהודה בן לקיש a different reason.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: It rejects the claim that the תנאים argue about טלטול מן הצד.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that רבי יהודה בן לקיש's permission could only come from holding that indirect moving is not moving. It ignored the special factor of a person's panic over his מת.
